what_its_for: Ustekinumab is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (a skin condition that causes red, scaly patches), psoriatic arthritis (joint pain and swelling related to psoriasis), Crohn's disease (inflammation of the digestive tract), and ulcerative colitis (inflammation of the large intestine). It works by calming down parts of your immune system that cause inflammation.
how_to_take: Ustekinumab comes as an injection given under the skin (subcutaneous) or as an infusion into your vein (intravenous) done by a healthcare provider. Your first dose for Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis is usually given as an IV infusion at a clinic or hospital. After that, you or a caregiver can give the injections at home under the skin. Always follow your doctor's instructions. Before injecting at home: wash your hands well, let the syringe or pen warm up at room temperature for 30 minutes, check that the liquid is clear and colorless (do not use if cloudy or has particles), choose a different spot on your body each time (thigh, stomach, or upper arm), and clean the skin with an alcohol wipe before injecting.
dosing: Your dose depends on your condition, your body weight, and how you respond to treatment. A typical schedule for psoriasis is one injection every 12 weeks after starting doses. For Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, the first dose is given by IV at a clinic, followed by an injection every 8 weeks. Always take the dose exactly as prescribed by your doctor — do not change your dose or schedule on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember, then ask your doctor when to take your next dose. Do not give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. It helps to mark your injection days on a calendar or set a reminder on your phone.
storage: Keep ustekinumab in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not shake the vial or prefilled syringe. If needed, you can store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 30 days, but after that it must be thrown away. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of used syringes and needles in a puncture-proof sharps container — do not throw them in the regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive live vaccines (such as the shingles vaccine Zostavax, live flu vaccine, MMR, or yellow fever vaccine) while taking ustekinumab, as it may make them unsafe or less effective. Talk to your doctor about which vaccines are safe for you. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, as this medicine affects your immune system and may make it harder to fight infections. Limit sun exposure and use sunscreen, as there may be a small increased risk of skin cancer. Tell your doctor before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, cough, painful urination, or wounds that do not heal; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; signs of nervous system problems such as numbness, weakness, vision changes, or seizures; unusual skin changes or growths; signs of heart failure such as sudden weight gain, swelling in your legs, or shortness of breath. Also tell your doctor if you have ever had tuberculosis (TB) or have been exposed to TB, as ustekinumab can reactivate it.
when_it_works: Ustekinumab works slowly. You may start to see some improvement in your skin or symptoms within a few weeks, but it may take 3 to 6 months to feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it even if you do not notice results right away — keep all follow-up appointments with your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks to the baby are not fully known, so your doctor will help you decide if this medicine is safe for you. Older adults: Older patients may have a slightly higher risk of infections. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: Ustekinumab is approved for children 6 years and older with plaque psoriasis. The dose for children is based on body weight. Liver or kidney problems: Let your doctor know if you have any liver or kidney conditions, as this may affect how the medicine is used.
